subject: Television & Streaming
title: Larry David and the Comedy of Discomfort
description: A micro-lesson that makes Larry David and the Comedy of Discomfort usable.

hook.text: Larry David co-created Seinfeld—the show about nothing—then made Curb Your Enthusiasm, a show about himself being.

buildup.text: David plays a fictionalized version of himself who says what everyone thinks but nobody should say out loud.

discovery.text: Curb is almost entirely improvised. David gives actors a scenario and lets them figure out the dialogue in real time.

twist.text: David is worth $400 million yet plays a character constantly annoyed by minor inconveniences. The gap is the joke.

climax.text: He proved that honesty is the funniest—and most dangerous—comedy tool. Saying the quiet part loud is his entire brand.

punchline.text: The richest man in comedy plays the most petty.

quiz.question: What unique production method does Curb Your Enthusiasm use?
